findings.title: No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock; the exclusive lock is held during file/CDN I/O
findings.body:
The read-lock fast path is released before `Lock()` is taken at line 48, and the cache is never re-checked after that. In a non-dev environment, if N requests arrive while the cache is still nil (startup, or after a failed load stored nil at line 69), all N miss. They queue on the write lock and each one re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` (line 60). The first load makes the others redundant. Repeat the `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` check right after `Lock()` and return the cached value if it is set.

In `setting.Dev` the cache is never used, so every call takes the exclusive lock for the whole file read, and for the CDN HTTP request if `cdn` is set (lines 55-57). Concurrent page renders in dev are therefore serialized on disk I/O. This is dev-only and low impact. The old code had a data race but no serialization. You could do the read outside the lock and take the lock only to store the result at line 69.

contracts.action: GetWebAssets now guards the package-level entryPointAssetsCache with an RWMutex: read lock for the fast path, write lock for the load and store.
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous code in the same function read `entryPointAssetsCache` unsynchronized and returned it when `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`. It otherwise reloaded the manifest and assigned the cache with no lock.
contracts.before_after: Before: the unlocked read and write were a data race under concurrent requests. After: the cache read and write are synchronized. The returned pointer is never mutated after it is stored, so sharing it is safe. The post-Lock re-check is missing, so concurrent cache misses each reload the manifest serially. The load logic at lines 54-70 is otherwise unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: None for users. The page still gets the same asset list. Concurrent cold-start requests do redundant manifest reads, and dev-mode requests are serialized.
contracts.failure_mode: If the load fails, `result` is nil and line 69 stores nil, as before. The error is returned to the caller and the next request retries. The defer unlock releases the write lock on all paths, including a panic. No deadlock: the RLock is released before Lock is taken.

summary: The RWMutex correctly removes the data race on `entryPointAssetsCache`, with no deadlock and correct unlock paths. The one note is a perf nit. The write lock is taken without re-checking the cache, so concurrent cold-start requests each reload the manifest. In dev, every request serializes on file I/O under the exclusive lock.
